title: Cap. X: Bellarmine — free-action participation; Confession XI; reatus vs habit
pass_a_gloss: Bellarmine proves it: whatever we say sticks in little ones from sin — guilt (reatus), or aversion, or privation of grace, or anything else — can in no way be given to them as vice, nor even exist, unless it has proceeded from a free action in which they somehow shared. Is that not to deny that hereditary vice inhering in infants is truly sin sufficient for damning them, as our Confession pronounces in Article XI? But let him go on. First: reatus is a relation following an action — how can it exist in one who is not a participant in the action? That argument would hold if there were no sin but actual sin, and no reatus except what immediately follows an action. But there is also habitual sin, and reatus following a habit.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's proof runs: whatever we say clings in little children from sin — guilt, aversion, loss of grace, or anything else — cannot be vice in them, cannot even exist, unless it came from a free act in which they somehow shared. Is that not to deny that the hereditary blot in infants is truly sin enough to damn them, as our Confession states in Article XI? Let him continue. First: guilt is a relation that follows an act — how can it stand in someone who had no share in the act? The argument would hold if the only sin were actual sin, and the only guilt what follows an act at once. But there is also habitual sin, and guilt that follows a habit.
source_text: Eam probat Bellarminus, Nam, inquit, quicquid dicamus in parvulis ex peccato haerere, sive reatum, sive aversionem, sive gratiae privationem, sive quid aliud; nullo modo parvulis vitio dari, ac ne esse quidem poterit, nisi processerit ab actione libera, cujus actionis illi aliquomodo participes fuerint. Nonne hoc est negare, vitium haereditarium, infantibus inhaerens, esse vere peccatum iis damnandis sufficiens, uti nostra pronunciat Confessio Artic. XI. Sed pergat. Nam primo, reatus, cum sit relatio consequens actionem, qui fieri potest ut existat in eo, qui non est particeps actionis? Valeret sane hoc argumentum, si nullum esset peccatum nisi actuale, nullus reatus nisi proxime actionem consequens. Nunc autem est etiam peccatum habituale, & reatus consequens habitum.

choices.decision: Bellarmine's demand denies hereditary vice as true damning sin vs Confession XI; Placeus distinguishes habitual sin/reatus
